statement.p: Find the center mass of the solid bounded by planes x+y+z=1, x=0, y=0, and z=0, assuming a mass density of \rho(x,y,z)=4 \sqrt{z}.

static.solution:
{x}_{CM}=\frac{\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 x\sqrt{z} \,dV}{\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 \sqrt{z} \,dV} {y}_{CM}=\frac{\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 y\sqrt{z} \,dV}{\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 \sqrt{z} \,dV}\qquad (\mathbf{1}) {z}_{CM}=\frac{\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 z\sqrt{z} \,dV}{\int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 \sqrt{z} \,dV} \mathcal{W} is the tetrahedron shown in the figure:
The projection \mathcal{D} of \mathcal{W} onto the xy-plane is the triangle determined by the line AB:y=1-x and the positive x and y axes.
The upper surface is the plane z=1-x-y and the lower surface is z=0.
Therefore, we describe \mathcal{W} by the following inequalities: 0\le x\le 1,\quad 0\le y\le 1-x, \quad 0\le z\le 1-x-y \qquad (\mathbf{2})
We compute the mass of the solid \mathcal{W}: \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 \sqrt{z} \,dV \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} \int_0^{1-x-y} 4 \sqrt{z} \,dz \,dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2}{3}{z}^{3/2} \bigg|_{z=0}^{1-x-y}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2}{3}{( 1-x-y )}^{3/2}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1 -\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{2}{5}{( 1-x-y )}^{5/2}\bigg|_{y=0}^{1-x}\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1-\frac{4}{15}\left({\left(1-x-(1-x)\right)}^{5/2}-{(1-x)}^{5/2}\right)\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1 \frac{4}{15}{( 1-x )}^{5/2} \,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\left(-\frac{4}{15}\cdot \frac{2}{7}{( 1-x )}^{7/2}\bigg|_0^1\right)\\ \amp =\amp 4\cdot\frac{4}{15}\cdot \frac{2}{7}= \frac{32}{105} \end{array} That is, \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 \sqrt{z} \,dV=\frac{32}{105} \qquad(\mathbf{3}) We now compute the triple integrals in the numerators of (\mathbf{1}). Using (\mathbf{2}) we have
\begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 x\sqrt{z} \,dV\amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} \int_0^{1-x-y} 4 x\sqrt{z} \,dz \,dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2x}{3}{z}^{3/2} \bigg|_{z=0}^{1-x-y}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2x }{3}{( 1-x-y )}^{3/2}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1\frac{2x}{3}\cdot\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right){(1-x-y)}^{5/2}\bigg|_{y=0}^{1-x}\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1\frac{-4x}{15}\left({\left(1-x-(1-x)\right)}^{5/2}-{(1-x)}^{5/2}\right)\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1 \frac{4x}{15}{( 1-x )}^{5/2} \,dx \end{array} We compute the integral using the substitution u=1-x, du=-dx. We get \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 x\sqrt{z} \,dV \amp =\amp 4\int_1^0 \frac{4}{15}( 1-u ){u}^{5/2} ( -\,du )\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1 \frac{4}{15}\left({u}^{5/2}-{u}^{7/2}\right) \,du\\ \amp =\amp 4\left(\frac{4}{15}\left(\frac{2}{7}{u}^{7/2}-\frac{2}{9}{u}^{9/2}\right)\bigg|_{u=0}^1\right)\\ \amp =\amp 4\left(\frac{4}{15}\left(\frac{2}{7}-\frac{2}{9}\right)\right)=\frac{64}{945} \quad(\mathbf{4}) \end{array} We compute the numerator of {y}_{CM} in (\mathbf{1}), using (\mathbf{2}). This gives \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 y\sqrt{z} \,dV \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} \int_0^{1-x-y} 4 y\sqrt{z} \,dz \,dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2y}{3}{z}^{3/2} \bigg|_{z=0}^{1-x-y}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2y}{3}{( 1-x-y )}^{3/2}dy \,dx\qquad (\mathbf{5}) \end{array} We compute the inner integral using the substitution u=1-x-y, du=-dy. We get \begin{array}{rcl} \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2y}{3}( 1-x-y )^{3/2} \,dy\amp =\amp \int_{1-x}^0 -4\cdot\frac{2}{3}( 1-x-u ){u}^{3/2} \,du\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2}{3}\left(( 1-x ){u}^{3/2}-{u}^{5/2}\right) \,du\\ \amp =\amp 4\left(\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{2(1-x)}{5}{u}^{5/2}-\frac{2}{7}{u}^{7/2}\right)\bigg|_{u=0}^{1-x}\right)\\ \amp =\amp 4\left(\frac{4}{15}( 1-x ){( 1-x )}^{5/2}-\frac{4}{21}{( 1-x )}^{7/2}\right)\\ \amp =\amp \frac{32}{105}{( 1-x )}^{7/2} \end{array} Combining with (\mathbf{5}) we get \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 y\sqrt{z} \,dV = \int_0^1 \frac{32}{105}{( 1-x )}^{7/2} \,dx=-\frac{32}{105}\cdot \frac{2}{9}{( 1-x )}^{9/2}\bigg|_0^1= \frac{64}{945}\qquad(\mathbf{6}) Finally, we compute the denominator of {z}_{\mathrm{CM}} in (\mathbf{1}), using (\mathbf{2}): \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{W}} 4 z\sqrt{z} \,dV\amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} \int_0^{1-x-y} 4 {z}^{3/2}dz \,dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2}{5}{z}^{5/2} \bigg|_{z=0}^{1-x-y}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_0^{1-x} 4\cdot\frac{2}{5}{( 1-x-y )}^{5/2}dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1 -\frac{2}{5}\cdot \frac{2}{7}{( 1-x-y )}^{7/2}\bigg|_{y=0}^{1-x}\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1-\frac{4}{35}\left({\left(1-x-(1-x)\right)}^{7/2}-{(1-x)}^{7/2}\right)\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\int_0^1\frac{4}{35}{( 1-x )}^{7/2}\,dx\\ \amp =\amp 4\left(-\frac{4}{35}\cdot \frac{2}{9}{( 1-x )}^{9/2}\bigg|_0^1\right)\\ \amp =\amp \frac{32}{315}\quad(\mathbf{7}) \end{array} Substituting (\mathbf{3}), (\mathbf{4}), (\mathbf{6}) and (\mathbf{7}) in (\mathbf{1}) we obtain the following center of mass: \left({x}_{\mathrm{CM}},{y}_{\mathrm{CM}},{z}_{\mathrm{CM}}\right)= \left(\frac{\frac{64}{945}}{\frac{32}{105}},\frac{\frac{64}{945}}{\frac{32}{105}},\frac{\frac{32}{315}}{\frac{32}{105}}\right)= \left(\frac{2}{9},\frac{2}{9},\frac{1}{3}\right)
